# COPYRIGHT & EDITORIAL CAUTION README

**Status:** Mandatory production policy for every video generated by Video Factory  
**Applies to:** Research, scripts, narration, images, footage, maps, graphics, music, subtitles, thumbnails, metadata and YouTube publishing  
**Default rule:** If the rights, source, accuracy or permitted use of an asset cannot be verified, **do not use it and do not publish the video**.

This document is an operational risk-control policy, not legal advice and not a guarantee that a video is infringement-free. Copyright law, platform rules, licences and permissions can vary by country and change over time. For a high-risk or disputed use, obtain qualified legal advice or written permission from the rights holder.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable principles

1. Create original reporting scripts, narration, graphics, maps, charts, animations and edits.
2. Report facts in our own words. Do not copy another publisher's article, headline, script, distinctive presentation, photographs, footage, graphics or audio.
3. Treat every third-party asset as **unapproved until its exact source and licence/permission have been checked**.
4. A credit, source link, disclaimer, crop, mirror, speed change, filter, pitch shift or short duration does **not** by itself grant permission.
5. Do not assume that material found through Google Images, YouTube, social media, a news website, Wikimedia Commons or an AI tool is free to reuse.
6. Keep evidence of where every external asset came from and why its intended use is allowed.
7. Stop publication if any mandatory check fails. Never silently replace a failed asset with an unverified one.
8. Do not promise “100% copyright-free”, “copyright-proof” or “guaranteed monetizable”. The system can reduce risk; it cannot eliminate all legal or platform risk.

## 2. News research: facts are not a licence to copy expression

News facts, dates, figures and events may be reported, but the source's original expression and media can still be protected.

### Allowed editorial workflow

- Use multiple reliable sources to establish what happened. Prefer primary sources for official facts: government departments, court orders, parliamentary records, police/public authority releases, regulators, scientific institutions and the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
- For significant or disputed claims, seek at least two independent sources. Record when only one primary source is available.
- Read sources for facts, then write a fresh script with a distinct structure, explanation and wording.
- Preserve exact quotations only when genuinely necessary, clearly marked and attributed. Keep quotations brief and assess whether permission or a legally valid exception is needed.
- Separate confirmed facts, allegations, estimates, opinions and developing information. Attribute allegations to the relevant named source and do not present them as established facts.
- Record source title, publisher/agency, URL, publication/update time, access time and the specific claims supported.
- Correct or withdraw a story promptly if a reliable update changes a material fact.

### Prohibited research shortcuts

- Do not copy/paste, translate paragraph-by-paragraph, lightly paraphrase or rewrite an article sentence-by-sentence.
- Do not reproduce a broadcaster's script, distinctive headline package, article structure or proprietary graphics.
- Do not use a source's paywalled article, subscriber-only content, database or feed in a way that breaches its terms.
- Do not bypass paywalls, access controls, robots restrictions or technical protections.
- Do not use another channel's video/audio as “research material” in the final edit.

**Source attribution is good editorial practice, but attribution alone is not permission to reproduce protected material.**

## 3. Visual assets: approval rules

### Preferred order

1. Original graphics, charts, maps, diagrams, typography and procedural animation created by this project.
2. Original AI-generated visuals, after checking the provider's terms and avoiding imitation of protected characters, brands, artists or identifiable people.
3. Public-domain or CC0 assets whose status and provenance have been checked.
4. Third-party assets with a clear licence or written permission that covers the intended use, including commercial YouTube publication where applicable.

### Licence checks

For every third-party image, video, sound or graphic, record and verify:

- Exact asset page URL (not only the direct download URL).
- Creator/author and rights holder, where available.
- Exact licence name and version, or written permission reference.
- Whether commercial use is allowed.
- Whether adaptations, cropping, overlays, subtitles and edits are allowed.
- Required attribution wording and placement.
- Any share-alike, notice, territory, duration or other conditions.
- Date checked and a saved copy/screenshot or other evidence of the licence terms.

### Creative Commons caution

- **CC0 / Public Domain:** Check that the work really is covered by the stated dedication/status and that no separate rights (such as privacy, publicity, trademark or third-party material) create additional restrictions.
- **CC BY:** Attribution and other licence conditions are mandatory.
- **CC BY-SA:** Attribution and share-alike obligations apply to adaptations; check compatibility before use.
- **CC BY-NC:** Do not use in this monetized/commercial-intent workflow.
- **CC BY-ND:** Do not use if the project will adapt, crop, remix, subtitle or otherwise modify the asset.
- **CC BY-NC-SA / CC BY-NC-ND:** Do not use.
- “Royalty-free” does not mean public domain or unrestricted. Read the actual licence and platform-specific restrictions.

Do not infer a licence from a search result snippet, filename, watermark, uploader statement alone or the fact that a file is downloadable.

### Never use without explicit permission or a verified legal basis

- TV news footage, broadcast recordings, news-channel screenshots or clips.
- Other YouTubers' videos, Shorts, livestreams, thumbnails or audio.
- Film, television, sports broadcast, music-video or OTT footage.
- Photographs copied from news publishers, agencies, social media or search engines.
- Brand/channel logos, proprietary lower-thirds, signature graphics or distinctive programme designs.
- Commercial stock assets whose licence does not cover the planned use.

Do not remove watermarks or attribution notices. Do not use a clip merely because it is short, transformed, blurred, mirrored or overlaid with narration.

## 4. AI-generated media

- Use only tools and accounts whose terms permit the intended generation and publication.
- Retain the tool name, generation date, prompt/project identifier where available, and the applicable terms/version.
- Do not prompt for a living artist's distinctive style, a protected character, a real person's likeness or a brand asset in a way that creates avoidable rights or impersonation risks.
- Do not generate a realistic image/video that falsely depicts a real person committing an act, making a statement, being arrested, injured or involved in an event.
- Label illustrative or reconstructed scenes clearly when viewers could mistake them for real footage. Never present synthetic visuals as actual event footage.
- Follow YouTube's altered/synthetic-content disclosure requirements when applicable.
- Human review is required for sensitive, political, public-safety, conflict, crime and disaster visuals.

## 5. Audio, narration and music

- Prefer project-generated narration using a voice and service whose terms allow the intended publication.
- Do not clone or imitate a real person's voice without documented authorization.
- Use original music, properly licensed music, or music whose licence explicitly permits the intended use.
- Do not assume a platform music library licence applies outside that platform or to every type of channel/video.
- Do not use film songs, commercial recordings, news audio, podcast clips or another creator's narration without permission or a verified legal basis.
- Keep licence receipts, track IDs, creator credits and attribution text.
- A voice generated by a TTS service does not make the script or underlying source material copyright-safe.

## 6. Maps, weather and data

- Prefer original maps and charts rendered from data, rather than screenshots of proprietary map or weather interfaces.
- Check the data provider's terms, attribution requirements, redistribution rights, caching limits and commercial-use conditions before displaying or republishing data.
- For weather, prefer official IMD bulletins and other authoritative meteorological sources. Record the issue time, valid period, geographic coverage and source URL.
- Clearly distinguish forecast, observation, warning and model estimate. Include the issue/update time and relevant location.
- Do not imply that a forecast is a guarantee. Preserve warning language and uncertainty.
- Do not copy proprietary map tiles, map screenshots, radar imagery or weather graphics unless their terms expressly allow the intended use.
- Do not present a generated weather graphic as an official IMD graphic. Label it as an independently prepared visual based on the cited data.

## 7. Editorial, privacy and defamation safeguards

Copyright clearance does not make a story safe or accurate.

- Verify names, dates, locations, numbers, quotations and context.
- Do not state an allegation as a proven fact. Use careful attribution and include relevant responses where reasonably available.
- Avoid sensational, misleading, hateful, discriminatory or needlessly graphic framing.
- Do not expose private personal information, home addresses, phone numbers, identity documents, medical details or private individuals' sensitive data without a lawful and editorially justified basis.
- Take special care with children, victims, witnesses, private individuals and people accused of crimes.
- Do not use a person's face, name or voice in a misleading synthetic context.
- For emergencies, health, public safety, communal tension, elections, courts and ongoing investigations, require enhanced human editorial review before publication.

## 8. Required provenance files for every video

Every production run must create and retain the following records alongside the MP4:

### `sources.json`

For every factual source:

- `publisher`
- `title`
- `url`
- `published_at` (if available)
- `accessed_at`
- `claims_supported`
- `source_type` (primary, official, news, research, other)
- `verification_notes`

### `asset_licenses.json`

For every external asset:

- `asset_id`
- `asset_type` (image, video, audio, font, map, other)
- `asset_page_url`
- `download_url` (if applicable)
- `creator`
- `rights_holder` (if known)
- `license_name_and_version` or `permission_reference`
- `commercial_use_allowed`
- `adaptation_allowed`
- `attribution_required`
- `required_attribution_text`
- `evidence_location`
- `checked_at`

### `credits.txt`

Human-readable credits and required attribution for the published video/description.

### `editorial_checklist.json`

Record research verification, script originality review, sensitive-content review, visual/audio clearance, technical checks and final approval status.

If any required record is missing, malformed or contradictory, mark the asset/video **BLOCKED**.

## 9. Automated fail-closed publishing gate

The production pipeline must use a fail-closed policy:

- Unknown, missing, ambiguous, expired or unverifiable licence → **REJECT ASSET**.
- Non-commercial or no-derivatives licence → **REJECT ASSET** for this workflow.
- Missing source URL, creator, licence evidence or required attribution → **REJECT ASSET**.
- News claim without adequate support → **HOLD STORY**.
- Material contradiction or unverified allegation → **HOLD STORY**.
- Missing weather timestamp/validity or geographic scope → **HOLD WEATHER SEGMENT**.
- Copyright/rights audit failure → **BLOCK VIDEO**.
- Editorial, privacy or safety review failure → **BLOCK VIDEO**.
- Failed technical validation or missing provenance files → **BLOCK VIDEO**.

No workflow may bypass these gates simply to meet a daily upload target. If a story or asset fails, replace it with an independently researched story or original graphic; never lower the standard.

### Required final status values

- `PASS`: all automated checks passed; still subject to any required human review.
- `HOLD`: more evidence or editorial review is needed; no upload.
- `BLOCKED`: prohibited or failed check; no upload.
- `PUBLISHED`: only after the publishing platform confirms the upload.

Automated checks are screening tools, not legal determinations. A human must review high-risk material and any uncertain licence or claim.

## 10. YouTube publishing and monetization

- Follow the current YouTube Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, copyright processes, monetization policies and altered/synthetic-content disclosure rules.
- Do not assume that permission to use an asset guarantees monetization eligibility.
- Avoid repetitive, mass-produced videos with little original value. Each bulletin should add original research, context, explanation, editorial judgment and meaningful visual treatment.
- Keep the source and licence records for each upload in case of a claim or review.
- During initial testing, upload as private/unlisted and inspect the result before enabling scheduled public release.
- Do not automatically dispute a Content ID claim. Review the claim, asset licence and evidence first; escalate uncertain cases for human/legal review.
- Never claim that a video is “copyright-free” merely because no Content ID claim appeared.

## 11. Incident response

If a claim, takedown notice, rights-holder complaint or credible correction is received:

1. Pause scheduled publication of affected videos/assets.
2. Preserve the video ID, source records, licences, receipts, correspondence and production manifest.
3. Identify the exact disputed material and all videos that reuse it.
4. Remove/replace the material where appropriate and regenerate the video.
5. Do not file a counter-notification or legal response automatically. It can have legal consequences; require human review and, where appropriate, qualified legal advice.
6. Record the resolution and update the asset blocklist/policy.

## 12. Pre-publication checklist

A video may proceed only when all applicable items are checked:

- [ ] Every important claim is sourced and checked.
- [ ] Script is independently written and not copied or mechanically paraphrased.
- [ ] Allegations, uncertainty and corrections are handled responsibly.
- [ ] Every external asset has verified rights and complete provenance.
- [ ] Every required credit/attribution is included.
- [ ] Music, narration, fonts and sound effects are cleared.
- [ ] Maps, weather data and charts comply with provider terms.
- [ ] Synthetic/reconstructed scenes are not misleading and are disclosed where required.
- [ ] Privacy, defamation, safety and sensitive-content checks are complete.
- [ ] `sources.json`, `asset_licenses.json`, `credits.txt` and `editorial_checklist.json` are present.
- [ ] Video/audio/subtitles pass technical quality checks.
- [ ] Required human review is complete.
- [ ] Publishing gate returns `PASS`.

## 13. Official policy references

Always re-check the current version before production; links and rules can change.

- [India Copyright Office](https://copyright.gov.in/) — Indian copyright law and official resources.
- [Copyright Act, 1957 (India Code)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/) — statutory text and amendments.
- [Creative Commons licences](https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/) — licence conditions and attribution guidance.
- [Creative Commons legal tools](https://creativecommons.org/public-domain/cc0/) — CC0 information.
- [Wikimedia Commons reuse guide](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Reusing_content_outside_Wikimedia) — asset-specific reuse and attribution.
- [YouTube Copyright](https://support.google.com/youtube/topic/2778546) — copyright claims and processes.
- [YouTube Channel Monetization Policies](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392) — monetization and inauthentic/reused content policies.
- [YouTube altered or synthetic content disclosure](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491) — disclosure guidance.
- [India Meteorological Department](https://mausam.imd.gov.in/) — official weather information.

**Final rule: Original first. Licensed only when verified. Uncertain means do not use. Failed audit means do not publish.**
